sector_notes: On 4 November, breadth improved (SPY +1.65%, DIA +3.10%, IWM +1.51%, QQQ +0.97%), but leadership was uneven and mega-cap names accounted for a large share of the S&P 500 advance. Financials, consumer discretionary, communication services, staples and healthcare led, while energy fell 4.74%, technology was flat and industrials declined 1.09%; over three sessions XLE was down 9.28% and XLK 1.68%, versus XLF +4.76% and XLY +6.02%. This is a rotation and dispersion regime rather than broad risk-on: favor liquid financials, selected industrials, healthcare and defensive consumer names, while avoiding energy and semiconductor/AI-infrastructure exposure until relative strength stabilizes.
